summary.text: A 10-year-old female patient with trisomy 21 had severe refractory obstructive sleep apnea despite previous surgery and failed non-invasive positive pressure ventilation. Baseline polysomnography showed a total apnea–hypopnea index of 35, an obstructive index of 35, a central index of 0.14 and a pulse oximetry nadir of 78. A drug-induced sleep endoscopy was done before hypoglossal nerve stimulator placement.

Hypoglossal nerve stimulator placement was performed within an investigational pilot trial. Anesthesia began with inhalation induction using sevoflurane before intravenous line placement, with sevoflurane maintenance and no paralytic. Table 2 lists fentanyl 1.82 mcg/kg and dexmedetomidine 0.65 mcg/kg. The patient received multimodal analgesia, local anesthetic from the surgeon and PONV prophylaxis, was extubated deep, was transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit, and was transferred to the floor for post-operative observation.

Table 3 lists an initial obstructive AHI of 35.0, a post-HNS value of 2.8 and a percentage change of 92.0. None of the patients experienced anesthetic complications, and all patients had notable improvement on follow-up polysomnography.

Baseline polysomnography showed a total apnea–hypopnea index of 36, an obstructive index of 34.3, a central index of 1.19 and a pulse oximetry nadir of 83.
